subject: mathematics
question_text: If |p| = 2, |q| = 3 and the angle between p and q is π/6, find |p × q|².

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 19, book p.71. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Computed twice. Direct: |p × q| = |p||q| sin θ = 2 × 3 × sin(π/6) = 6 × (1/2) = 3, so |p × q|² = 9. By the identity |p × q|² = |p|²|q|² − (p·q)²: p·q = 2 × 3 × cos(π/6) = 6 × (√3/2) = 3√3, so (p·q)² = 27 and |p|²|q|² − (p·q)² = 36 − 27 = 9. The two routes agree, and the second route is put on the page as the fourth step because a four-mark question on a one-line substitution needs the identity to be worth its marks. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the four separate acts: stating the magnitude formula, substituting and squaring, computing the dot product, and confirming through the identity. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors carries a Section B slot on the paper and also appears in Section C. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the square of the cross-product magnitude from the two lengths and the angle — name each move in order.

steps.label: Write the magnitude formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. The cross product carries SIN of the angle; the dot product carries cos. Writing the wrong one here is the single most common way this question is lost.
steps.memory_tip: Cross product goes with sin, dot product goes with cos.

recall.must_convey: That |p × q| = |p||q| sin θ, with sin and not cos.
accept: the magnitude of the cross product is mod p mod q sin theta
cross product uses sine of the angle
write the formula with sin theta not cos theta
cross product ki sin theta, dot product ki cos theta
mod p into mod q into sin theta

steps.why: The cross product measures the area of the parallelogram on the two vectors, and that area depends on the perpendicular height, which is the sine of the angle.
common_mistakes: Using cos θ, which belongs to the dot product.
Writing p × q as a number when only its magnitude is a number.

steps.label: Substitute and square
steps.margin_note: Second mark. sin(π/6) = 1/2 is a standard value. The question asks for the SQUARE, so squaring is part of this step, not an afterthought.

recall.must_convey: That sin(π/6) = 1/2, so |p × q| = 3 and |p × q|² = 9.
accept: sin pi by six is a half so the magnitude is three
two times three times a half is three and squaring gives nine
the square of the cross product magnitude is nine
sin pi by six half, so magnitude three, square nine
substitute thirty degrees and square the result

steps.why: The question asks for the square, so the answer is already available here. The remaining marks go to proving it a second, independent way.
common_mistakes: Stopping at |p × q| = 3 and never squaring.
Using sin(π/6) = √3/2, which is sin 60°, not sin 30°.

steps.label: Find p·q for the check
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The check needs the dot product, so compute it from the same two lengths and the same angle, this time with cos.
steps.memory_tip: Same lengths, same angle, but cos this time: cos(π/6) = √3/2.

accept: cos pi by six is root three by two so the dot product is three root three
the dot product squared is twenty seven
compute p dot q with the cosine of the same angle
cos pi by six root three by two, p dot q three root three
three root three squared is twenty seven

steps.why: The identity that will confirm the answer contains the dot product, so it has to be computed first. It also shows that the same pair of vectors carries both products at once.
common_mistakes: Using sin(π/6) here, which belongs to the previous step.

steps.label: Confirm with the identity
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The identity |p × q|² = |p|²|q|² − (p·q)² follows from sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and it reproduces the same 9 from completely different arithmetic.

recall.must_convey: That |p × q|² = |p|²|q|² − (p·q)² = 36 − 27 = 9, matching the direct answer.
accept: the identity gives thirty six minus twenty seven which is nine
mod p squared mod q squared minus the dot product squared
both methods give nine so the answer is confirmed
thirty six minus twenty seven nine, rendu methods same
the identity comes from sin squared plus cos squared equals one

steps.why: Squaring |p||q| sin θ and |p||q| cos θ and adding gives |p|²|q|², so the two products are tied together. That tie is what lets one answer check the other without repeating the same arithmetic.
